articles.text: TĀNGMǓ: Ài! Shì nǐ ya! Hǎo jiǔ bu jiàn! Jīntian zěnme yǒu shíjiān chūlai zǒuzou?
TOM: Well, it's you! I haven't seen you in a long time! How is it you've got time to come out for a walk today?
LǏ PÍNG: Yíge zhōngtóu yǐqián, wǒ cóng xuéxiào gěi ni dǎ diànhuà, nǐ bú zài jiā. Gāngcái wǒ dào zhèli fùjìn mǎi dōngxi, jiù lái kànkan. Zhēn bú cuò, nǐ yǐjing huílai le.
LǏ PÍNG: I called you an hour ago from school, but you weren't home. I just came over to this neighborhood to do some shopping, so I stopped by to visit. It's great that you're back already.
TĀNGMǓ: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ gāngcái dào péngyou jiā jiè shū qu le.
TOM: Sorry. I just went over to a friend's house to borrow a book.
LǏ PÍNG: Shénme shū? Yòu shi guānyú Zhōngguóde ba?
LǏ PÍNG: What book? More about China, I bet.
TĀNGMǓ: Duì le, yǒu Xiānggǎngde, dàlùde, yě yǒu Táiwānde, dōu shi xiǎoshuōr. Nǐ zuòxia kàn, wǒ qù gěi ni dào bēi chá lai.
TOM: Yes, there are ones from Hong Kong, the mainland and Taiwan, all fiction. Sit down and have a look. I'll go get you a cup of tea.
LǏ PÍNG: Bú yào máfan, shénme hēde dōu xíng.
LǏ PÍNG: Don't go to any trouble. Anything to drink is fine.
TĀNGMǓ: Kěkǒukělè, júzi shuǐr, háishi píjiǔ?
TOM: Coke, orange juice or beer?
LǏ PÍNG: M, júzi shuǐ ba!
LǏ PÍNG: Um, orange juice.
TĀNGMǓ: Hǎo, wǒ mǎshang jiù lái. Yào bīngkuàir ma?
TOM: Okay, I'll get it right now. Do you want ice cubes?
LǏ PÍNG: Bú yào, xièxie.
LǏ PÍNG: No, thanks.
LǏ PÍNG: Tāngmǔ?!
LǏ PÍNG: Tom?
TĀNGMǓ: Ng?
TOM: Yeah?
LǏ PÍNG: Zhè sānge dìfangde shū, nǐ dōu kàn. Nǐ juéde zěnmeyàng?
LǏ PÍNG: Reading books from all three of these places, what do you think?

TĀNGMǓ: Wǒde gǎnjué bú shi yíjù huà kěyi shuōqīngchude. Èng... zhème shuō ba, wǒ zǒng juéde dàlù rén, Xiānggǎng rén, hé Táiwān rén dōu shi Zhōngguo rén, tāmen yǒu yíyàngde wénhuà chuántǒng, kěshi yīnwei zhèngzhìde qíngkuàng bù tóng, shèhuìde qíngkuàng yě jiù bù yíyàng le.

TOM: I can't explain my feelings in just a few words. Hmm... let's say that I've always felt that people on the mainland, in Hong Kong and in Taiwan are all Chinese, all have the same cultural tradition, but because the political situations are different, the social situations are also different.
LǏ PÍNG: Nǐ shuōde duì, dànshi nǐ yào dǒngde Zhōngguo shèhuì, zhǐ kàn shū shi bú gòude.
LǏ PÍNG: You're right. But if you want to understand Chinese society, it's not enough just to read books.

TĀNGMǓ: Ēi, nǐ zhīdao ma, xiànzài xué Zhōngwénde xuésheng yǒu hěn duō jīhui dào Zhōngguo qù. Suǒyǐ wǒ jìhua zài zhèige xuéqī wánlede shíhou, qù Zhōngguo kànkan. Érqiě, wǒ hái xiǎng zhǎo ge hǎo péngyou yìqǐ qù.

TOM: Say, you know, students of Chinese have a lot of opportunities to go to China now. So I'm planning to go to China for a visit when this semester is over. And what's more, I'd like to find a good friend to go with.

LǏ PÍNG: Zuótian wǒ jiēdào wǒ mǔqinde xìn, tā xīwàng wǒ huí Xiānggǎng guò shǔjià. Zěnmeyàng, nǐ hé wǒ yìqǐ huíqu ba. Nǐ kěyi zhù zài wǒmen jiāli. Érqiě, zài Xiānggǎng yìfāngmiàn nǐ yǒu jīhui hé Zhōngguo rén tán huà, yìfāngmiàn kěyi zhīdao dàlù, Xiānggǎng hé Táiwānde qíngkuàng. Nǐ kàn hǎo bu hǎo?

LǏ PÍNG: Yesterday I got a letter from my mother, and she'd like me to come back to Hong Kong for summer vacation. How about going back with me? You can stay at our house. What's more, in Hong Kong, on the one hand you'll have a chance to talk with Chinese and on the other hand you can learn about the situation on the mainland, in Hong Kong and in Taiwan. What do you think?
TĀNGMǓ: Fēicháng hǎo!
TOM: Great!
LǏ PÍNG: Nàme, nǐ hái yào hé nǐ jiāli rén shāngliang yíxiàr ba?
LǏ PÍNG: Well then, you'll still want to discuss this a bit with your parents, I suppose?
TĀNGMǓ: Bú bì. Gěi fùmǔ dǎ diànhuàde shíhou, gàosu tāmen wǒde jìhua jiù xíng le. Wǒ yào yánjiū Zhōngguo shèhuì, fùmǔ yídìng huì gāoxìngde.
TOM: That's not necessary. When I call them, I'll tell them my plan, and then everything should be all right. I'm sure they'll be happy that I want to study Chinese society.
LǏ PÍNG: Měiguo niánqīng rén dōu yǒu zìjǐde xiǎngfǎ. Zhèi yìdiǎnr, wǒ fēicháng xǐhuan.
LǏ PÍNG: Young people in America really think for themselves. I really like that.
TĀNGMǓ: Niánqīng rén yǒu zìjǐde xiǎngfǎ shi duìde, kěshi fùmǔde huà yě yīnggāi kǎolǜ.
TOM: It's good that young people think for themselves, but you still ought to consider what your parents say.
LǏ PÍNG: M. Nà wǒmen shuōhǎo le, jīnnián shǔjià qù Xiānggǎng. Xiànzài hái yǒu wǔge yuède shíjiān kěyi zhǔnbèi.
LǏ PÍNG: Mm. Well then we have decided. This summer vacation we'll go to Hong Kong. We still have five months to prepare.
TĀNGMǓ: Duì, jiù zhème bàn! Jīnnián xiàtian wǒ jiù yào dào zhèige dìfang dà, rénkǒu duō, lìshǐ yòu chángde guójiā qù le. Hāi! Zhèige jìhua zhēn ràng wǒ gāoxìng!
TOM: Right, that's what we'll do. This summer we will go to that country with a large area, a great population, and a long history. Boy, this plan really makes me happy!
LǏ PÍNG: Hǎo, jiù zhèiyàng. Wǒ yīnggāi zǒu le!
LǏ PÍNG: Good, it's settled. I have to go.
TĀNGMǓ: Nǐ máng shénme! Hái zǎo ne!
TOM: What's the hurry? It's still early!
LǏ PÍNG: Bù zǎo le, huíqu hái děi niàn shū ne!
LǏ PÍNG: No it isn't. I still have to study when I get back.
TĀNGMǓ: Nà, yǒu shíjiān nǐ zài lái wánr!
TOM: Well then, come again when you have time!
LǏ PÍNG: Hǎo, míngtian jiàn.
LǏ PÍNG: Okay, see you tomorrow.
TĀNGMǓ: Míngtian jiàn!
TOM: See you tomorrow!
